description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background.

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- If the file is outside the working directory, you must Read it in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

schema.name: Edit
schema.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- If the file is outside the working directory, you must Read it in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default false)

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task
tools.description:
Withdraw a background-task chip you previously created with spawn_task.

Call this when a suggestion you flagged is now stale, superseded, or irrelevant — e.g. you (or the user) already fixed it in this session, or you spawned a better-scoped replacement. To replace a chip: call spawn_task with the new suggestion first, then dismiss the old task_id.

Only chips the user hasn't acted on can be withdrawn from the queue. If the user already started or dismissed the task, the result says so (a dismissed task's copy kept for later is withdrawn too) — do not retry.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

 * under the reviews and the versions; the ratings and counts carried nothing at
 * all. None of it survives. The version dropdown went with them: it never
 * chose anything — the installer always takes the latest compatible build.
 *
 * What IS real and now leads instead: the category, the upstream source with a
 * link to the mod's own page, whether it is featured in our catalogue, its
 * install state on THIS server, and the installer's own error text when a
 * install fails. Those come from the DB and from worker/game-mods.ts.
 *

content.thinking:
The SQL side looks fine since Prisma parameterizes queries, but I'm noting the unbounded search could cause a heavier scan under load and there's no rate limiting—both minor issues. Also checking the tag matching for case sensitivity concerns, though it's not a big deal.

The bigger issue is pagination: requesting page=9999 still returns 200 with a self-referencing canonical and page-specific title, but reuses content from the last real page, creating infinite duplicate indexable URLs beyond the actual page count—that's a medium severity SEO problem. Edge cases like negative, fractional, or zero-padded page numbers all normalize correctly to canonical URLs, so those are fine, but the metadata title should clamp to the real max page or redirect/404 instead of trusting the raw query param. I also note all paginated pages share the same meta description, which is a minor duplicate-content concern.

Beyond pagination, the blog has no category or tag filtering—categories are just plain spans, tags are spans like #seobatch—so with 346 posts across 29 pages, users can only browse chronologically or search, missing out on valuable SEO hub pages like "Minecraft server guides." That's a medium-priority gap for both SEO and UX.

On mobile, I'm cataloging several real issues: a layout blowout on posts with many items due to a min-content grid (high severity given 36% mobile traffic on high-intent guides), CTAs buried extremely far down the page—nearly 7 viewports deep on some posts and no sticky CTA on the blog index (high impact on conversion), a hero section eating up to 75% of the mobile viewport before content appears (medium-low), and inline images lacking explicit width/height causing layout shift since they're lazy-loaded without reserved space.

I also verified card images on the index use proper aspect-ratio containers, avoiding CLS there. Separately, I found a site-wide CSP issue blocking Meta Pixel's fbevents.js—I confirmed this is a genuine browser CSP enforcement error (not caused by my own route interception) since next.config.ts's script-src is missing connect.facebook.net, and the ConversionTags component is indeed rendering the pixel. This ties into an existing memory note about needing to fix Meta Pixel SPA re-firing, so it's a high-priority, cross-cutting problem even though it's technically outside blog scope.

Now I'm compiling performance numbers: the blog index loads fast at ~0.1s/151KB HTML, while post pages are TTFB-dominated at 0.26-0.31s with 130-155KB HTML and duplicated article content in the RSC payload. Playwright shows healthy total transfer sizes (~341KB) and load times once accounting for wait time, but images are a real problem—raw PNGs with no caching, no next/image optimization, and an oversized 2208px-wide pricing-plans.png being served to 390px phone screens. I also noted the getPublishedPost double-fetch isn't memoized, and the blog index's force-dynamic setup re-runs count and ILIKE search queries on every view, which is acceptable for now.

On the internal linking side, product-linking to per-game routes is inconsistent: 29 posts link to /minecraft-server-hosting but none link to /free-minecraft, and CTAs point to generic marketing pages instead of deep-linking into the deploy wizard with a preselected game family—something the middleware already supports and could boost conversions. content.text:
I found 6 High, 9 Medium and 7 Low issues on the blog. The top two are a mobile layout bug on about 33 guide pages and made-up 5-star ratings on every post. There are no broken links and the sitemap is complete. Posts come from the `BlogPost` table only (`prisma/schema.prisma:2499`), with 346 published. The index uses `app/blog/page.tsx` and `lib/blog.ts`. Posts use `app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx`, which calls `renderArticle()` (a hand-written markdown renderer in `lib/blog.ts:461`) and the `BlogPostView.tsx` client component. `BlogArticle.tsx` and `data.ts` only serve the noindexed `/preview/blog-post` page. I used 65 sequential curls, plus one Playwright run of 4 page loads at 390×844. That run blocked every non-GET request and the Facebook/Google trackers, and replaced `sendBeacon`. Nothing under /opt was changed. ## High **1. About 33 posts are wider than the phone screen, so the whole page zooms out.** - **Cause:** the post body grid is `rail grid` (`BlogPostView.tsx:267`). The `
` at line 319 has no `min-w-0`. The body div (361–364) and the inline `code` style (`lib/blog.ts:213`) have no `overflow-wrap`. So one long file path sets the column width. - **Measured:** on `/blog/how-to-install-cs2-plugins-metamod-counterstrikesharp`, `scrollWidth` was 615 on a 390 viewport, with the article at 595px wide. In mobile-emulation mode `innerWidth` became 615, so a real phone shows the page at about 63% scale. - **Scope (estimated from the text, not loaded):** about 33 posts, mostly game "set up a dedicated server" guides. The longest token is 71 characters (`/home/palworld/server/Pal/Saved/Config/LinuxServer/PalWorldSettings.ini`). About 31 more are borderline. - **Fix:** add `min-w-0` to the article (or use `grid-cols-[minmax(0,1fr)]`), and `[overflow-wrap:anywhere]` on the body and on `code`. **2. Every post shows invented 5-star ratings.** - `` appears three times on every post: the author card (`BlogPostView.tsx:393`) and both product panels (`:511`, next to "Instant deploy · full root · 24/7 support"). - The live HTML carries `aria-label="5 out of 5 stars"` on all 346 posts. This breaks the rule against made-up numbers. - **Fix:** remove them. **3. About 28 posts claim a "one-click Mods manager" for games the installer doesn't support.** - The installer only covers minecraft, rust, valheim, ark, unturned, dst, squad, soulmask, projectzomboid, tf2, l4d2 and empyrion (`lib/mod-install-support.ts:30-56`). Palworld is excluded on purpose. - Posts still promise it, along with an "EAC toggle" and "drag load order", for Factorio, Enshrouded, V Rising, Satisfactory, tModLoader, 7 Days to Die, Garry's Mod, Conan Exiles and Palworld. Minecraft posts also promise CurseForge/FTB modpack installs, but CurseForge isn't a supported source. - These include the 12 newest posts (all of `/blog` page 1). Readers who buy on the strength of this will be disappointed. - **Fix:** rewrite those paragraphs game by game to match what actually works. **4. On a phone, the first sales link comes very late.** - The table of contents and its product box are desktop-only (`hidden lg:block`, line 270). The first template call-to-action comes after the whole article (line 367), and the blog has no sticky button. - Measured first link to a product page: | Page | Position | Page height | |---|---|---| | Subnetting post | 5,747px (about 6.8 screens down) | 8,903px | | CS2 post (a link inside the text) | 3,976px | 7,407px | | `/blog` index | 6,394px, and it points to `/register` | 7,595px | - The post header alone takes 591–629px of the 844px screen (`min-h-[52vh] pt-28`, line 211). - **Fix:** put a product link right after the Quick answer box, add a sticky bottom bar on mobile (`StickyCTA.tsx` already exists), and shorten the header on mobile. **5. The product links in posts are generic, not matched to the topic.** - `productLinkForPost` (`lib/blog.ts:123-158`) only picks between 5 hub pages. - **Minecraft:** all 43+ Minecraft posts go to `/game-servers`. None go to `/minecraft-server-hosting` or `/free-minecraft`, and no post links to `/free-minecraft` at all. - **Other games:** every game post goes to `/game-servers`, even though each game has its own page and all of those return 200. - **Newest game guides go to VPS:** 6 of them (CS2, Project Zomboid, Garry's Mod, 7 Days to Die, Terraria, Satisfactory) point to `/vps` "Cloud VPS hosting". This was confirmed live on the CS2 post. - **Email:** 8 email posts go to `/domains`, because the "domain" check (line 139) runs before the "email" check (line 145). - **Fragile matching:** it matches substrings, so words like "ark" or "rust" inside other words can misfire. - **Wrong copy:** the "Deploy in seconds" headline and the "full root" claim also appear on the domain and email panels. - **Fix:** map each game to its own page (and add a free-Minecraft link), and link straight into the deploy wizard with the product and game preselected. **6. (Site-wide, found in the console) The Content Security Policy blocks the Meta Pixel.** - `next.config.ts:25` `script-src` doesn't include `https://connect.facebook.net`, but `ConversionTags.tsx:53` loads `fbevents.js`. - The browser reported a policy violation on all 3 pages I loaded. So browser-side Pixel events don't fire anywhere on the site. - **Fix:** add the domain to `script-src`. ## Medium **7. The markdown renderer leaves raw syntax on the page.** - Literal `*italics*` show in 138 of 346 posts, e.g. "*persistence*" on the Minecraft SMP post. - Markdown tables show as rows of `|` characters in 4 posts: vps-vs-shared-vs-dedicated, subnetting, cpanel-vs-plesk, shared-hosting-vs-vps-which-to-choose. - Blockquotes show a literal ">" in 3 posts. - A literal `**` shows in 1 post, and numbered lists restart at "1." after code blocks in 6–7 posts. - **Fix:** switch to a real markdown parser with sanitizing (tables wrapped in `overflow-x-auto`), or add italic, table and blockquote support. **8. "Related guides" is the same on every post in a category.** - `getRelatedPosts` (`lib/blog.ts:100`) returns the 3 newest posts in the category. All 133 Gaming posts, including the Minecraft SMP one, show Factorio, Factorio and Unturned. - 113 of 346 posts have no links from other posts. The oldest post is 29 pages deep in the index. - **Fix:** rank related posts by shared tags and title words. **9. Out-of-range page numbers create endless indexable duplicates.** - `/blog?page=9999` returns 200 with the page-29 posts, but canonical is `/blog?page=9999`, the title says "page 9999", and robots is `index, follow`. - The cause is that `generateMetadata` uses the page number as requested rather than the clamped one (`page.tsx:56-63`). - `page=0` and `page=abc` are fine: 200, page 1, canonical `/blog`. The total is correct: 346 posts, 29 pages, 10 on the last page. Normal pages point to themselves as canonical, which is correct. - **Fix:** use the clamped page in the metadata, and 404 or redirect past the last page. **10. Most posts have no social-share image.** - 146 posts, including all 33 newest, plus `/blog` itself, have no `og:image`, no `twitter:image` and no image in the structured data. They still declare `summary_large_image`. - The 200 posts that do have covers share 8 product screenshots; 82 of them use `deploy-wizard.png`. - **Fix:** generate a per-post share image with `next/og`. **11. 104 posts show publish dates earlier than the blog existed.** - These posts were created 2026-07-23 to 07-25 but show publish dates from 2026-04-25 to 07-24. The dates are hard-coded in the seed scripts (e.g. `prisma/seed-blog-vps.ts:30`). The repo's first commit is 2026-07-23. - These dates appear in the byline, `article:published_time` and the structured data. - The "Last updated" field reflects bulk script runs, not edits: 200 posts show 2026-08-05, the image backfill date. - **Fix:** set the publish date to the real creation date. **12. 11 pairs of near-duplicate posts compete for the same searches.** - Examples: `how-to-set-up-a-cs2-server` vs `…counter-strike-2-dedicated-server`, and the palworld, valheim, satisfactory, v-rising, ark-asa, 7dtd, zomboid, enshrouded, bedrock and nextcloud pairs. Two pairs have identical titles. - **Fix:** merge each pair and 301-redirect the loser. **13. An internal tag is shown to readers.** - The `seobatch` tag is on 233 posts and appears as a "#seobatch" chip and as an `article:tag` meta tag (confirmed live). - **Fix:** filter internal tags out. **14. The "Quick answer" box isn't an answer.** - It shows the excerpt (`[slug]/page.tsx:70`), which is already printed as the intro line just above it. It's a teaser ("Want a persistent survival world…? Here's how…"), which wastes the box for ChatGPT-sourced readers. - The FAQ structured data also absorbs the closing sales paragraph into the last answer (seen on the SMP post); up to 111 posts may be affected. **15. There are no category or tag pages.** - There are 12 categories and 478 tags, but the category labels aren't links and `/blog/category/gaming` returns 404. This misses hub pages like "Minecraft server guides". ## Low - **16. Search:** it runs on the server over the whole database (`?q=`), and Prisma's `contains` is parameterized, so it's safe from SQL injection. Search pages are noindexed with canonical `/blog`. But results are sorted by date, not relevance: `q=minecraft` returns 57 results, 6 of the 12 on page 1 don't have "Minecraft" in the title, and "set up a vanilla Minecraft server" is result #21. There is no length limit on `q`, and `searchPublishedPosts` (`lib/blog.ts:28`) is unused code. - **17. Images:** - All 9 distinct images return 200 and none is over 500KB. - They are plain `` tags, not next/image, served as PNG with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=0`. The largest, `pricing-plans.png`, is 336,864 bytes at 2208px wide and is sent to phones as is. - Inline images have no width or height (`lib/blog.ts:507`), so the page shifts as they load. - **18. Performance is fine:** | Page | Time | HTML size | |---|---|---| | `/blog` | 0.106s | 150,965 B | | minecraft-smp | 0.260s | 154,795 B | | vps-vs-shared | 0.280s | 130,423 B | | cs2-plugins | 0.308s | 137,994 B | About 341 KB is transferred per page over 21–23 requests. Small wins: - The article HTML is sent twice (once in the page, once in the client data). - `getPublishedPost` runs twice per view without caching. - Every post page is rendered fresh on each request (`force-dynamic`). - **19.** 95 page titles are over 60 characters including " — Nxeon", and 33 meta descriptions are over 160. - **20.** `/preview/blog-post` is public (200, noindex, nofollow) and shows "4.9 / 5 from wipe admins", a fake author "Mara Voss" and made-up prices (`BlogArticle.tsx:636`, `data.ts:120,151-154`). - **21.** `llms.txt` doesn't mention the blog at all, even though ChatGPT is 52% of first visits. ## Checked and fine - **Links:** all 274 distinct internal link targets in post bodies work. The 233 blog links match the database, and all 41 other pages returned 200. No in-page anchors are broken. - **Sitemap:** `/sitemap.xml` points to `/sitemap/0.xml`, which lists `/blog` and all 346 posts, exactly matching the database. - **Post page basics:** each post has a title, meta description, canonical, `BlogPosting` and `FAQPage` structured data, date, author and reading time. There are no "demo" badges or placeholder text. Everything I collected is in `/tmp/claude-0/-root/ec6fa978-d80b-4147-9982-eea470598e2c/scratchpad/mkt/blog/`. That includes `posts.json`, `rendered.json` (all 346 posts run through a copy of the renderer), `link_status.txt`, `mobile_results.json` and `mobile_cs2.mjs`.
